claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial interfaces produce high stress concentrations.
The proposed treatment uses a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K will topologically transform the lamellar interfaces into coherent FCC/B2 boundaries.
The coherent FCC/B2 interfaces form through pressure-induced stacking-fault rearrangement and thermal activation.
The FCC phase is mechanically softer than the hard B2 phase.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces allow dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
Dislocation transfer across the coherent interfaces alleviates interfacial stress concentration.
High pressure stabilizes the FCC phase at elevated temperature in CoCrFeMnNi-related alloys.
Stacking faults and twinning will operate as synergistic deformation mechanisms in HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The combined deformation mechanisms will homogenize strain and reduce stress concentration.
The treated alloy will develop a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces.
The treated alloy will show elongated crack propagation associated with ductile fracture rather than isolated microcracks.
At high strain, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge.
Conventional annealing or lower-pressure HIP retains incoherent interfaces and produces brittle fracture with isolated microcracks in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The selected pressure and temperature are sufficient to produce the proposed transformation while remaining below the threshold for phase instability or eutectic decomposition.
The boundary condition involves an hcp-fcc-fcc coherent transition.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies coherent FCC/B2 interfaces, whereas the boundary describes an hcp-fcc-fcc transition and does not account for the B2 phase; these are inconsistent descriptions of the proposed transformation pathway.
